metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Passaic County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Rifle Camp & Garret Mountain Section, West Paterson Historic Core & McBride Corridor
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 3.435%, with an equalization ratio of 66.11%.
Public education represents 52.4% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 31.8%.
Average residential assessment is $337,161, producing an average annual tax bill of $11,581.48.

neighborhoods.name: Rifle Camp & Garret Mountain Section
neighborhoods.character: Elevated scenic neighborhood bordering 1,000-acre Garret Mountain and Rifle Camp county parks with custom homes
neighborhoods.description: Scenic residential section nestled against county parkland reservations, offering woodland views and modern suburban homes.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Top tier residential ratables supporting Woodland Park municipal operations.

neighborhoods.name: West Paterson Historic Core & McBride Corridor
neighborhoods.character: Traditional community center with cape cods, split-levels, and two-family homes near Passaic River and McBride Ave retail
neighborhoods.description: Historic town core (formerly West Paterson borough) convenient to shopping plazas and Route 46 commercial ratables.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Strong commercial tax base along Route 46 / McBride Ave offsets residential municipal burden.

equityAnalysis.summary: Woodland Park Borough maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Woodland Park Borough, homeowners pay an average of $11,581.48 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 11.01% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 66.11%, assessed values average ~66.11% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 52.4% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 31.8%, and Passaic County claims 15.8%.
